result.title: PROVISO: Provenance-Informed Action Selection for Secure LLM Agents
result.summary: LLM agents act on the external world through tools and third-party skills, so a single executed action can cause irreversible harm. Existing defenses judge a proposed action without tracking whether its content comes from the user or from external sources such as tool outputs, and they judge it in isolation rather than against an available alternative, which forces a trade-off between security and utility. We present PROVISO, a controller that decides which action to commit after the agent proposes an action and before it is executed. PROVISO encodes trusted observations, external observations, the proposed action, and an alternative into provenance-typed memory, relates them through role-specific queries, and commits the action with the highest calibrated value learned from outcomes. On four agent security tasks spanning the agent lifecycle, no baseline exceeds PROVISO in both security and utility. PROVISO improves F1 over the strongest baseline by 13.84 points on SkillsBench and by 7.07 points on ToolSafe, and it reaches 88-99 F1 on three additional skill detection benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PROVISO 控制器，在 LLM agent 执行动作前，将可信观察、外部观察、候选动作及替代动作编码为带来源类型的记忆，经角色特定查询比较后，按从结果中学到的校准价值提交动作。
AI.relevance_reason: 其来源类型记忆与价值校准的动作提交机制，或可供核查 LVR 中证据来源筛选及 STOP／候选选择决策的借鉴，但任务与视觉推理相距较远。
